title: Real-Time Fraud Detection
summary: Fraud detection decides, in under 100 milliseconds and while the customer waits, whether a payment looks like the real cardholder. It looks up behaviour features computed from recent activity, scores them with a model, and applies business rules; uncertain cases go to human analysts. The hard part is learning: the truth (a chargeback) arrives weeks later.

walkthrough.title: Payment arrives
walkthrough.text: Checkout calls the risk API synchronously with the transaction: amount, card fingerprint, device ID, IP, email, and merchant. The whole decision has a budget of about 50 to 100 milliseconds.

walkthrough.title: Look up features
walkthrough.text: Precomputed signals are fetched in a few milliseconds: how many cards this device used in the last hour, distance between IP and billing address, account age, and the email's history across merchants.

walkthrough.title: Score with the model
walkthrough.text: A gradient-boosted model turns roughly 200 features into a fraud probability, such as 0.87.

walkthrough.title: Apply rules
walkthrough.text: Rules combine the score with business policy: block lists, per-merchant thresholds, and 'send to 3-D Secure if score > 0.6 and amount > $500'.

walkthrough.title: Route borderline cases
walkthrough.text: High-value orders in the grey zone are held and queued for an analyst instead of being auto-declined.

walkthrough.title: Respond
walkthrough.text: Checkout receives approve, challenge (3-D Secure), review, or decline, plus reason codes it can log.

walkthrough.title: Collect the truth
walkthrough.text: Chargebacks arrive 30 to 90 days later, and analyst verdicts arrive within hours. Both become labels joined back to the original features.

walkthrough.title: Retrain and deploy
walkthrough.text: A new model trains on the latest labels, runs in shadow mode against live traffic, then takes over gradually once its precision and recall beat the current one.

data.label: Checkout / Payment Request

output.name: Risk request
output.type: JSON: { txnId, amount, cardFingerprint, deviceId, ip, email, merchantId }

responsibilities: Collects device and behaviour signals in the browser or app before the payment is submitted.
Calls the risk API with a strict timeout and acts on the decision.
Shows a 3-D Secure challenge instead of a hard decline for medium-risk payments.

failureModes.impact: Checkout must choose between lost sales and unscreened payments.
failureModes.mitigation: Per-merchant fallback policy, e.g. approve under $100, otherwise send to 3-D Secure.

failureModes.scenario: Device signals blocked by privacy tools
failureModes.impact: Fewer features, so the model is less certain.
failureModes.mitigation: Model trained with missing-feature patterns; missing data alone is never a block reason.

data.label: Risk Decision API

output.name: Lookups
output.type: Feature keys: card, device, IP, email, merchant

responsibilities: Orchestrates feature lookup, scoring, and rules within a hard latency budget.
Logs every decision with the exact feature values used, so training data matches what the model saw.
Publishes each transaction as an event so streaming jobs update the features for the next one.

failureModes.scenario: Training features computed differently from serving features
failureModes.impact: The model looks great offline and performs poorly in production (training/serving skew).
failureModes.mitigation: Train on the logged serving-time features, not features recomputed later.

failureModes.scenario: One slow dependency eats the whole budget
failureModes.impact: Every decision falls back to the default policy.
failureModes.mitigation: Per-call deadlines; score with partial features rather than wait.

data.label: Model Scoring Service
responsibilities: Scores a feature vector in about 5 milliseconds.
Runs the live model and one or more shadow models side by side on the same traffic.
Returns the top contributing features so analysts and merchants see why.

failureModes.scenario: Fraudsters adapt to the model (concept drift)
failureModes.impact: Fraud rate climbs within weeks of a new pattern appearing.
failureModes.mitigation: Monitor score distributions and fraud rate daily; retrain frequently.

data.label: Real-Time Feature Store
responsibilities: Serves precomputed velocity counters and reputation features in single-digit milliseconds.
Updated continuously by streaming jobs that consume every transaction event.
Keeps sliding-window counts (1 minute, 1 hour, 24 hours, 30 days) per card, device, IP, and email.

failureModes.impact: Velocity counters miss the last few minutes; a card-testing burst looks normal.
failureModes.mitigation: Alert on lag in seconds; increment the hottest counters synchronously in the API.

failureModes.scenario: Hot key from one merchant or IP
failureModes.impact: One shard overloaded; lookups time out.
failureModes.mitigation: Key salting for known hot keys, local caching, and replicas.

data.label: Rules & Policy Engine
responsibilities: Turns a probability into an action using thresholds tuned to each merchant's appetite for risk.
Lets analysts ship rules within minutes to stop a new attack before the model learns it.
Sends grey-zone, high-value cases to manual review.

failureModes.scenario: Hundreds of overlapping rules nobody understands
failureModes.impact: Good customers declined for reasons no one can explain.
failureModes.mitigation: Rule owners, expiry dates, and backtesting each rule against labelled history.

failureModes.impact: A typo declines all payments in a country.
failureModes.mitigation: Shadow-run new rules and cap their impact (e.g. alert if a rule hits > 1% of traffic).

data.label: Manual Review Queue
responsibilities: Shows analysts the evidence: linked accounts, device graph, order history.
Prioritizes by amount and time to shipment, so goods aren't sent before a decision.
Produces fast labels within hours instead of the 30 to 90 days chargebacks take.

failureModes.scenario: Queue backs up during a sale
failureModes.impact: Held orders miss shipping cut-offs and customers cancel.
failureModes.mitigation: Auto-decide cases past their SLA by policy; adjust thresholds to control queue volume.

failureModes.scenario: Analysts only see what the model flags
failureModes.impact: Labels are biased toward the model's existing beliefs.
failureModes.mitigation: Review a small random sample of approved transactions too.

data.label: Labels (Chargebacks & Verdicts)
responsibilities: Joins each outcome to the features that were logged at decision time.
Tracks label maturity: recent transactions are 'unknown', not 'legit'.
Separates fraud chargebacks from 'friendly fraud' and service disputes.

failureModes.impact: The model learns that new fraud patterns are fine.
failureModes.mitigation: Only train on transactions old enough for chargebacks to have arrived.

failureModes.impact: The model can't learn whether its declines were right (selection bias).
failureModes.mitigation: Approve a tiny random holdout of would-be declines to measure true outcomes.

data.label: Training & Deployment Pipeline

output.name: Model release
output.type: Model artifact + version → shadow → canary → live

responsibilities: Trains on time-based splits (train on past months, test on the latest), never random splits.
Compares candidates on precision at the operating threshold and dollars of fraud caught.
Promotes models gradually: shadow mode, then a small traffic share, then all traffic.

failureModes.impact: Future information leaks into training; offline metrics are too good to be true.
failureModes.mitigation: Strictly time-ordered splits and leakage checks on every feature.

failureModes.impact: Thresholds tuned for the old model suddenly decline twice as many customers.
failureModes.mitigation: Recalibrate scores and re-tune thresholds in shadow before promotion.
